Uniform circular motion repeats at equal intervals, so it is periodic. It is not to-and-fro about a mean position, so it is not oscillatory.
f = ω/2π = 10π/2π = 5 Hz; in 3 s the particle makes 5 × 3 = 15 oscillations

NCERT defines oscillatory motion as periodic to-and-fro motion about a mean position. So A is true, R is true, and R explains A (strictly damped oscillations are not periodic, but NCERT's statement is the intended one).
I is correct: displacement can be an angle, a pressure change or a field. II: T = 1/50 = 0.02 s, but ω = 2π × 50 = 100π rad/s, not 50 rad/s, so II is incorrect.
e^{-ωt} decays monotonically and never repeats, so it is non-periodic. The other three are sums or powers of sinusoids, which are periodic.
Amplitude = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
sin²(πt) = (1 − cos 2πt)/2. Angular frequency is 2π, so the period is 2π/2π = 1 s.
A: √2 sin(ωt + π/4) is SHM with period 2π/ω (II). B: (1 − cos 2ωt)/2 is SHM about mean 1/2 with period π/ω (III). C is periodic but not SHM (IV). D is non-periodic (I).

A is true: cos²ωt = (1 + cos 2ωt)/2, period π/ω. B is false: a sum of two different frequencies is not SHM. C is true. D is false: log ωt is not periodic. E is true by Fourier's theorem. So A, C and E.
x = A sinωt, so v = Aω sin(ωt + π/2) and a = Aω² sin(ωt + π). Acceleration leads velocity by π/2.
Speed is zero at the extremes, so A is false. |a| = ω²A is maximum at the extremes, so R is true.
I: A/2 = A sin(2πt/T) gives t = T/12 = 2.4/12 = 0.2 s, so I is correct. II: a = −ω²x, so the slope is negative and II is incorrect.
T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g, so the period is unchanged on the Moon.
Each third has k = 3×60 = 180 N/m. Two in parallel give 180 + 180 = 360 N/m.
Single spring: 2π√(m/k), so A-II. Vertical spring: mg = kΔl, so m/k = Δl/g, giving B-IV. Series: k_eff = k1k2/(k1+k2), giving C-III. Parallel: k_eff = k1+k2, giving D-I.

A is true: the period is independent of amplitude. B is false: gravity shifts the equilibrium position but not the period. C is false: each part has constant nk. D is true: restoring force constant = ρAg, so T ∝ 1/√ρ. E is true: series k_eff is less than either k. So A, D and E.
ω = 10π, so f = 5 Hz. KE goes as cos^2, so it varies at 2f = 10 Hz.
KE has period T/2, so A is false. R is true: KE is maximum at the mean position, which is passed twice per cycle.

E = (1/2)mω^2A^2, so doubling frequency gives 4E; I is true. For II, v^2/ω^2 + x^2 = A^2 is an ellipse that becomes a circle when ω = 1 rad/s, i.e. k = m numerically in SI units. II is likely intended true, though strictly 'speed' (non-negative) gives only half an ellipse.
In a lift accelerating upward, g_eff = g + g/3 = 4g/3. T' = 2/√(4/3) = √3 = 1.73 s.
ΔT/T = ½(Δl/l) = 0.1%. The clock runs slow and loses 0.001 × 86400 = 86.4 s.
Upward lift: g+a, so IV. Downward lift: g−a, so I. Free fall: g_eff = 0, no oscillation, so II. Horizontally accelerating car: g_eff = √(g²+a²), so III.

A is true. B is false: effective length runs to the centre of the bob. C is true: standing raises the centre of mass, shortening the effective length. D is false: g is smaller on the Moon, so T is larger. E is true: the formula holds only for small amplitudes.
v ∝ √T, so doubling v needs 4T: T = 4 × 300 K = 1200 K = 927 °C
A: P/ρ is constant at fixed T, so v is unchanged (II). B: v ∝ √T, so 4T gives 2v (IV). C: v ∝ 1/√μ, so 4μ gives v/2 (I). D: v ∝ √T_tension, so 9× tension gives 3v (III).

A true: Newton's isothermal value is ~280 m/s. B true: Laplace's adiabatic formula. C false: moist air is less dense, so sound is faster in it. D false: frequency stays the same and wavelength changes. E true: speed is generally highest in solids, lowest in gases.
Comparing with y = a sin(kx - ωt): k = 4π and ω = 200π. So v = ω/k = 50 m/s. The form (kx - ωt) means the wave moves along +x.
Maximum particle speed = aω = 0.004 × 400 = 1.6 m/s. Wave speed = ω/k = 400/50 = 8 m/s. Ratio = 1.6/8 = 0.2.

Maximum particle speed is aω, while wave speed is ω/k. These are equal only if ak = 1, so A is false in general. For R: ∂y/∂t = -aω cos(kx - ωt) and -v ∂y/∂x = -(ω/k)(ak cos(kx - ωt)), which is the same expression. So R is true.
I: Intensity is proportional to A²f², so doubling both gives 16 times, not 4 times. I is incorrect. II: v = 600π/2π = 300 m/s, and the (kx + ωt) form means motion along -x. II is correct.
The phase difference is π/2, so the amplitudes add in quadrature: A = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 mm.
Amplitude ratio is √9 : √1 = 3 : 1. Imax : Imin = (3+1)² : (3−1)² = 16 : 4 = 4.
Adding the waves: a[sin(kx−ωt) + sin(kx+ωt)] = 2a sin kx cos ωt. At x = 0, sin kx = 0, so x = 0 is a node.
Resultant amplitude is R = 2a cos(φ/2). φ = 0 gives 2a (III); φ = π gives 0 (II); φ = π/2 gives √2a (IV); φ = 2π/3 gives a (I).

A is true: rigid-boundary reflection gives a phase change of π. B is false: a pulse is not inverted at a free end. C is true: frequency is unchanged on reflection. D is true: waves pass through each other unaffected. E is false: destructive interference gives |a1 − a2|. So A, C, D are correct.
For a string fixed at both ends, f1 = v/2L = 200/(2×0.5) = 200 Hz.
Closed pipe: f1 = v/4L = 340/3.4 = 100 Hz. Only odd harmonics occur, so the second overtone is the 5th harmonic = 500 Hz.
4 antinodes means 4 loops, so L = 2λ and λ = 0.6 m. Then v = fλ = 250×0.6 = 150 m/s.

A is true: closed pipe f = v/4L, open pipe f = v/2L. R is also true as a general fact. However, A follows from the end boundary conditions (displacement node at the closed end, antinode at the open end), not directly from R. So R does not explain A.
7th harmonic: L = 7λ/4. Displacement nodes lie at 0, λ/2, λ and 3λ/2 from the closed end, giving 4 nodes, so I is correct. A standing wave has no net energy transport, so II is incorrect.
The beat frequency is the difference of the two frequencies: |260 - 256| = 4 beats per second.

The unknown fork is 384 ± 6, so it is 378 or 390 Hz. Wax lowers its frequency. If it were 390 Hz, lowering it moves it toward 384 Hz and the beats decrease, which matches. So the original frequency was 390 Hz.
The beat frequency is 504 - 498 = 6 Hz. The time between successive loudness maxima is the beat period, 1/6 s.

A: beats per second = |ν1 - ν2| (II). B: the tone heard is the average frequency, (ν1 + ν2)/2 (III). C: wax adds mass and lowers the frequency (IV). D: filing removes mass and raises the frequency (I).

A is true: beats are distinguishable only for a difference of about 10 Hz or less. B is true: the heard tone is 303 Hz with 6 beats per second. C is false: if wax increases the beats, the unknown fork had the lower frequency. D is true: beat period = 1/|ν1 - ν2|. E is false: filing raises the frequency. So A, B and D are correct.
